chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Dawud al-Abzari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
A caller cries out every day, 'O son of Adam, build for death, amass for annihilation, and construct for destruction!'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the call to 'son of Adam' regarding death and destruction in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the concept of *al-dam* (the call to death) as a daily spiritual reminder for believers to detach from worldly accumulations. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *dhikr al-mawt* (remembrance of death) not merely as a fear-inducing event, but as a transformative practice that reorients one’s purpose toward the eternal afterlife. The 'herald' symbolizes the internal and external cues that prompt reflection on the transient nature of material wealth and status.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 2.Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from al-Ḥakam ibn Ayman, from Dāwūd al-Abzārī, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “
A caller cries out every day, ‘O son of Ādam, beget for death, amass for annihilation, and build for destruction!’”
